analysis.title: DeskTalk - High stakes into APEC summit, early thoughts
key_insights: APEC summit takes place Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen, China. The last Trump-Xi meeting was in September. Nvidia developments and a possible Putin attendance raise the summit's significance. The official schedule is not out.
Nvidia puts US-China chip policy in focus. H200 chip sales to China are currently allowed with a 25% import tariff. Citi sees a high risk of tighter restrictions on China's access to advanced chips.

Axios reports Commerce Secretary Lutnick recently met with Treasury, Defense and State Department principals about chip export concerns. Citi Research writes some measures, such as FCC rules, need no congressional or presidential authorization and can be invoked immediately.
China extended the suspension of the 24% additional tariffs on US imports for two months until Jan 9 and kept the 10% blanket tariff. The US extended Section 301 tariff exemptions to Jan 9.

US companies still report lower rare earth volumes despite last year's truce. FT reports Japan asked the US to urge China to ease rare earth export controls. Xi and Trump are expected to meet again in Florida next month.

Putin proposed a US-China-Russia trilateral meeting last month. Confirmed attendance, the first since 2017, would be a constructive signal. Taiwan participates this year, and Taiwan assets underperformed overnight after Xi said complete reunification is inevitable. China could act as a mediator on Iran.
Citi expects substantial deal progress to be unlikely. Geopolitical and AI uncertainty should keep headline risk elevated. Nvidia earnings and a potential major IPO fall next week.
Nvidia has meaningfully dragged tech sentiment. US inflation and Fedspeak amid elevated oil has been the biggest driver for rates and FX markets.

market_movers.rationale: Risk of tighter US export restrictions on advanced chips to China is high. Nvidia has dragged tech sentiment and reports earnings next week.

sector_views.rationale: Chip export control risk and AI uncertainty keep headline risk elevated, and Nvidia has weighed on tech sentiment.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earnings are due next week, with no figures or estimates given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: China extended the suspension for two months, so the trade truce holds through early January.
